newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet /AT&T deal is missing jigsaw piece.
newsitem.headline: Stet /AT&T deal is missing jigsaw piece.

text.p: A global telecoms alliance between Italy's Stet and AT&T Corp of the United States announced on Wednesday is a key strategic piece for both parties in the increasingly competitive telecoms jigsaw, analysts said.
State telecoms holding company Stet is entering a global strategic alliance with AT&T with a focus on Latin America and Europe. It is also to join the AT&T-Unisource telecoms venture in Europe.
"Unisource needed access to the French and Italian markets and it's getting it now," said a London-based telecoms analyst who declined to be named.

"For Stet, it's getting an American partner and it's also reaffirming its position in Europe. Stet had three options -- it was either AT&T, Concert or Global One so it's basically the missing piece of the jigsaw puzzle," the analyst said.

Concert brings together British Telecommunications Plc, MCI Communications Corp of the U.S. and Spain's Telefonica. Global One is an international joint venture involving Sprint Corp, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom.
Michael Pacitti, equity analyst at James Capel in London, said: "This is not a particularly momentous event for AT&T, it is more important for Stet which needs a global partner."
"It will help Stet, which is heavily concentrated in Europe, to expand abroad," Pacitti added.

Gianni Allavena, head of equity research at Milan brokers Intersim, said in terms of industrial strategy, the link-up was positive. "From a long-term strategic point of view it should be positive given that Stet was the only one in Europe that did not yet have a major international link," he said.
"In terms of the financial impact it's too early to say," Allavena added.

Analysts also noted the accord gave Unisource potential access to Spanish markets. Stet is currently in a consortium with Spanish firms bidding for Spain's second domestic telephone operator Retevision.
Stet is due to merge with fixed line operator Telecom Italia on July 18 ahead of its planned privatisation, which is expected to take place in October.

Pacitti noted Wednesday's agreement could be significant in view of the forthcoming privatisation, saying: "It will be important if AT&T takes an equity stake in Stet -- ahead of the Stet-Telecom Italia share placement later this year."
In Rome, Industry Minister Pierluigi Bersani said the accord led "to the possibility that there could be significant international partners in the privatisation process".

Under the agreement as outlined so far, the AT&T/Stet joint venture in Latin America will be 50-50 owned by the two partners and will deliver a portfolio of global services via two newly formed pan-American operating entities.
The accord with Unisource, a joint venture grouping Dutch PTT, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT, puts Stet in its 60-40 percent AT&T-Unisource venture with AT&T.

Stet plans to take a significant stake in AT&T-Unisource Communications Services (AUCS), distributing its services in Italy and transferring into AT&T-Unisource the relevant business activities of Stet's data and telecoms unit Telemedia International.
Stet will also have the option to take a shareholding of up to 30 percent of AUCS. Stet is due to hold a news conference to illustrate the deal at 1500 GMT.
